name: Charlemagne
hook: The Frankish king crowned emperor on Christmas Day 800, with a paladin epic and a cheese named in his honor.

facts.label: Holy Roman Emperor
facts.statement: Charlemagne was king of the Franks; on Christmas Day in 800, in Rome, Pope Leo III crowned him Holy Roman Emperor.

facts.label: Charles Martel
facts.statement: Charles Martel, nicknamed "the Hammer," was Charlemagne's grandfather; he stopped the Moors at the Battle of Tours in 732.

facts.label: Pepin the Short
facts.statement: Pepin the Short, or Pepin III, was Charlemagne's father; Charlemagne's brother Carloman inherited titles alongside him.

facts.label: the Carolingian dynasty
facts.statement: The Carolingian dynasty is named for Charlemagne; in France it ended in 987 with the death of Louis V, his descendant.

facts.label: Roland
facts.statement: Roland, Charlemagne's vassal, dies in a Saracen ambush in the 12th-century Song of Roland after refusing to blow his olifant for help.

facts.label: Roquefort
facts.statement: Roquefort, the blue cheese made from French ewes' milk, was supposedly a favorite of Charlemagne.

facts.label: Pippin
facts.statement: Pippin, a 1972 musical about Charlemagne's son, won Ben Vereen a Tony; the character finds he has "Magic to Do" in Italy.
